How to play Rage Bait

Reach the exit in each room to clear the level and unlock the next one. That sounds easy until a cliff gives way, a saw rolls into your path, or the exit moves as you approach it. Rage Bait is a free browser game with 310 levels across ten stages. The first course has six ledges. By the end of Stage 1, you’ll tackle 40-ledge courses that can take you from hills and tunnels to water crossed by boat.

Use the status line under the game to see your current objective. In some rooms, reaching the door is only half the puzzle. You might need to carry an apple to a tree, touch switches in order, or jump into a button overhead to open a passage. Your campaign progress saves in this browser, and the Stages panel lets you replay any level you’ve unlocked.

Controls

  • Use A and D or the left and right arrow keys to move. On a phone, hold either on-screen arrow.
  • Press Space, W, or the up arrow to jump or swim. On a phone, tap Jump for a jump or a swim stroke.
  • Press R or use Restart to start the current level again.
  • Choose Full screen for more room to see the route and use the touch controls.

Frequently asked questions

How do I get past surprise traps?

Pause on solid ground and watch your next landing. Some spikes switch position or timing after you die, so check the ledge again before repeating a jump. If a cliff collapses, look for a smaller ledge below it. A crack in the ground or a warning flash can give you time to move.

Why is the exit locked or moving?

Read the status line for a pickup, delivery, or switch sequence. If the exit relocates, check where it landed and plan the route back before jumping. In rooms with size-changing pads, try shrinking for a low passage or getting bigger to reach an overhead switch.

Do I ever run out of lives?

No. You have unlimited retries. A death sends you back to the first room of the current level. If you want a timed run, the Daily Challenge offers one course that changes at midnight UK time. You can share your time and death count after finishing.
